title: Execution-path calibrator for token-phase kernel switching
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Different kernel implementations (e.g., tiled attention, fused QKV, custom decode kernels) have wildly different cost/latency trade-offs depending on two orthogonal axes: hardware fingerprint (SM count, memory bandwidth, tensor core availability) and token-phase characteristics (long prefill bursts vs. many short decode steps). Existing static routing and coarse heuristics cause p95 spikes and suboptimal throughput for mixed workloads (chat + batching).

Goal: Implement an execution-path calibrator that observes short rolling traffic windows per-VM and per-model to automatically pick and swap in kernel implementations between prefill and decode phases. The calibrator should: (1) make architecture-aware initial recommendations using an offline fingerprint catalog, (2) perform safe online micro-exploration with rollback on regression, (3) maintain an exploration budget to avoid destabilizing hot paths, and (4) surface telemetry for ops and model teams.

Scope: Prototype runtime component + control-plane policy + basic console telemetry. The prototype targets x86+NVIDIA and AWS-G5/G4 classes (first pass).
acceptance_criteria: Calibrator can switch kernel implementation at prefill/decode boundary without breaking model correctness (unit tests + integration tests pass)
Observed 95th percentile latency reduced by >= 10% for mixed chat workload in our internal benchmark suite (compare baseline runtime-1.19)
Micro-exploration mechanism rolls back within 1s of detected regression above configured SLO thresholds
Calibrator exposes per-model per-node decisions and cost delta in Console for at least the last 24h
A documented fallback matrix exists and is validated against offline microbenchmarks for targeted hardware classes
tasks: Spike: build offline fingerprint catalog generator (arch -> recommended kernels) (owner: Marcus)
Implement calibrator control-loop in runtime (observe -> propose -> trial -> commit/rollback)
Add safe rollback and abort conditions tied to p50/p95/p99 SLOs
Instrument telemetry (decision traces, latency/cost deltas) and add Console widget mockup
Run cluster canary on 10% of dedicated pool for 2 days, collect regression signals
Create integration tests and perf suite for prefill vs decode switching
Write design doc and run architecture review with infra and research
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: exploration could increase tail latency for critical traffic; Mitigation: strict budget & immediate rollback on SLO violations
Risk: fingerprint mismatch across cloud instance families; Mitigation: conservative default catalog + force-lookup microbench on first boot
Risk: increased complexity in tracing; Mitigation: bounded trace sampling and aggregated decision metrics
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Spike, 2w): catalog generator + paper design; internal microbench baseline
Phase 1 (Prototype, 4w): runtime calibrator with synthetic trials; unit/integration tests
Phase 2 (Canary, 1w): 10% dedicated traffic + ops dashboard; monitor for regressions
Phase 3 (Gradual rollout, 2w): widen to 50% then 100% with aggressive telemetry gating
comments: 2025-01-10 Sofia Patel: Kickoff — scoped spike to validate that kernel microbenchmarks can predict runtime behavior for short decode steps. Linked design stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/ExecPath+Calibrator

2025-01-22 Marcus Green: Offline catalog generator prototype completed. Initial mapping shows fused-QKV preferred on G5 for prefill >512 tokens; tiled-attn wins for decode-heavy workloads. See benchmark: https://internal-bench/redwood/runtime/execpath/spike-20250122

2025-02-05 Marcus Green: Runtime prototype implemented (control-loop + trial harness). Pushed initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1532 — needs review from infra and perf teams.
2025-02-18 Leah Ortiz (perf): Reviewed PR and requested stronger rollback invariants and test harness for transient noise. Added card to extend test harness.
2025-02-25 Marcus Green: Canary scheduled for 2025-02-28 on shard 'dedicated-us-west-2-3' with 10% traffic. Dashboard mock: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/execpath-calibrator

2025-03-03 Ops: Canary day 3 — slight p99 blip correlated with a model that performs heavy attention slicing; rollback triggered and new conservative threshold applied. Logged incident: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-20250303-14
notes: Design decisions: prefer conservative defaults on first rollout and rely on fast microbench as a warmstart; avoid expensive full-model reprofile in canary.
Followups: extend catalog to AMD + A100 families, add quantized-kernel fingerprint, and integrate with autoscaler to consider throughput targets when switching kernels.
